learn.hook: A school has 100 lockers and 100 students. Student 1 opens every locker, student 2 flips every 2nd locker, student 3 flips every 3rd... At the end only a few lockers are open. Which ones? The square numbers!
points: A square number is a whole number multiplied by itself: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, ... We write 7 × 7 as 7² and read it as '7 squared'.
A square number can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9. So a number ending in 2, 3, 7 or 8 is never a perfect square.
Adding odd numbers from 1 builds squares: 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 = 4². The sum of the first n odd numbers is n².
Between n² and (n + 1)² there are exactly 2n numbers that are not squares.
Factors come in pairs (2 × 18 = 36). In a square number one pair is a number with itself (6 × 6), so a square number has an odd count of factors. That is why only square-numbered lockers stay open!

example.q: How many non-square numbers lie between 9² and 10²?

learn.reallife: A chessboard has 8 × 8 = 64 small squares. Square floor tiles, rangoli dot grids and seating in a square hall all use square numbers.

quiz.q: Which of these is a perfect square?
quiz.explain: 18 × 18 = 324. The others end in 8, 2 and 7, and squares never end in those digits.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the last-digit rule for squares

quiz.q: What is 1 + 3 + 5 + ... + 19 (the first 10 odd numbers)?
quiz.explain: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n². Here n = 10, so the sum is 10² = 100.
steps: Odd numbers from 1 to 19: there are 10 of them
quiz.mistake: Counts only 9 odd numbers, or multiplies 10 by 19

quiz.q: How many non-square numbers are there between 15² and 16²?
quiz.explain: Between n² and (n + 1)² there are 2n non-square numbers. 2 × 15 = 30 (they are 226 to 255).
quiz.mistake: Includes one of the end squares in the count

quiz.q: Meena arranges 36 laddoos in a square tray with equal rows and columns. How many laddoos are in each row?
quiz.explain: A square arrangement needs rows = columns. 6 × 6 = 36, so each row has 6 laddoos.
steps: Find a number that times itself makes 36
quiz.mistake: Halves 36 instead of finding its square root

quiz.q: A perfect square can NEVER end in which digit?
quiz.explain: Squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6 or 9. For example 1² = 1, 4² = 16, 3² = 9. No square ends in 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 6 or 9 cannot be the last digit of a square

quiz.q: What is (0.3)²?
quiz.explain: 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09. Squaring means multiplying the number by itself, not doubling it.
steps: One decimal place + one decimal place = two decimal places
quiz.mistake: Doubles the number or puts the decimal point in the wrong place

quiz.q: How many factors does 49 have?
quiz.explain: The factors of 49 are 1, 7 and 49. The pair 7 × 7 gives only one factor, so the count is odd: 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts 7 twice, or forgets it

quiz.q: In the locker game with 50 lockers and 50 students, how many lockers stay open at the end?
quiz.explain: Only lockers with square numbers stay open: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49. That is 7 lockers.
quiz.mistake: Thinks half the lockers stay open

teach.ask: Gappu flaps: Why does a square number like 36 have an odd number of factors? Explain it to me!
teach.praise: Wow! Factors make pairs, but the square root pairs with itself, so one is left over. Odd! I get it now!
teach.nudge: But how do factors usually come — alone or in pairs? And what happens with 6 × 6?

learn.hook: Arjun's square garden has an area of 196 m². How long is each side? Finding a square root is like running the squaring machine backwards!
points: The square root is the opposite of squaring: √81 = 9 because 9² = 81.
Prime factor method: write the number as primes, make pairs of equal primes, and take one prime from each pair. 324 = (2 × 2) × (3 × 3) × (3 × 3), so √324 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 18.
Subtraction trick: keep subtracting 1, 3, 5, 7, ... If you reach 0 after n steps, the number is n².
If a prime has no partner, multiply (or divide) by it to get a perfect square.
Estimating: √50 is between 7 and 8 because 49 < 50 < 64, and it is closer to 7.

example.q: Find the smallest number by which 72 must be multiplied to get a perfect square.

learn.reallife: When a carpenter knows a square tabletop's area and needs the side, or when you plan a square rangoli of 400 dots, you use square roots.

quiz.q: What is √576?
quiz.explain: 576 = 2⁶ × 3². Taking one from each pair gives 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24, and 24 × 24 = 576.
quiz.mistake: Halves the number instead of taking the square root

quiz.q: What is the smallest number by which 180 must be multiplied to get a perfect square?
quiz.explain: 180 = (2 × 2) × (3 × 3) × 5. Only 5 has no partner, so multiply by 5: 180 × 5 = 900 = 30².
quiz.mistake: Picks a prime that is already in a pair

quiz.q: By which smallest number should 252 be divided to get a perfect square?
quiz.explain: 252 = (2 × 2) × (3 × 3) × 7. Dividing out the lonely 7 leaves 36 = 6².
quiz.mistake: Divides by a prime that is already paired

quiz.q: Harpreet subtracts 1, 3, 5, 7, ... from 64, one after another. After how many subtractions does she reach 0?
quiz.explain: 64 = 8², and n² is the sum of the first n odd numbers, so it takes 8 subtractions.
quiz.mistake: Halves 64 instead of using square roots

quiz.q: Between which two whole numbers does √70 lie?
quiz.explain: 8² = 64 and 9² = 81. Since 64 < 70 < 81, √70 is between 8 and 9.
quiz.mistake: Thinks √70 is about 70 ÷ 10 = 7

quiz.q: Arjun's square garden has an area of 196 m². How long is one side?
quiz.explain: Area of a square = side × side. 14 × 14 = 196, so the side is 14 m.
quiz.mistake: Divides the area by 4 or by 2 instead of taking the square root

quiz.q: What is √(4/9)?
quiz.explain: Take the square root of the top and the bottom: √4 = 2 and √9 = 3, so the answer is 2/3. Check: (2/3)² = 4/9.
quiz.mistake: Takes the root of only the top or only the bottom

quiz.q: What is √1.44?
quiz.explain: 1.2 × 1.2 = 1.44. A number with 2 decimal places has a square root with 1 decimal place.
steps: 1.44 has 2 decimal places, so the root has 1
quiz.mistake: Halves 1.44 or misplaces the decimal point

teach.ask: Gappu tilts his head: How do I find √144 using prime factors? Please show me the trick!
teach.praise: Pairs of primes, one from each pair, multiply! √144 = 12. You are a great teacher!
teach.nudge: After breaking 144 into primes, how do you group them? And what do you take from each group?

topics.title: Cubes, cube roots and the taxi number

learn.hook: When the great mathematician Ramanujan was told a taxi's number, 1729, looked boring, he smiled: it is the smallest number that is a sum of two cubes in two different ways!
points: A cube number is a number multiplied by itself three times: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64. A big cube with side 4 is built from 64 small unit cubes.
Cube root is the reverse: ∛343 = 7. With prime factors, make groups of three equal primes and take one from each group.
Odd numbers make cubes too: 1 = 1³, 3 + 5 = 2³, 7 + 9 + 11 = 3³, 13 + 15 + 17 + 19 = 4³.
1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³. It is called the Hardy–Ramanujan number.

example.q: Is 1728 a perfect cube? If yes, find ∛1728.
steps: Groups of three: (2×2×2), (2×2×2), (3×3×3) — nothing left over

learn.reallife: Ice cubes, dice and Rubik's cubes are cubes. A 3 × 3 × 3 Rubik's cube looks like 27 small cubes stacked together.

games.title: Cube facts
items: The cube of an odd number is always odd.
odd × odd × odd is always odd, e.g. 3³ = 27.
Every cube number ends in 0, 1, 5 or 6.
Every number ending in 3 has a cube ending in 7.
The last digit of the cube depends only on the last digit: 3 × 3 × 3 = 27, so it ends in 7.
1729 can be written as a sum of two cubes in two different ways.
A solid cube of side 3 units is made of 9 unit cubes.
It needs 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 unit cubes; 9 is just one layer.

quiz.q: What is ∛512?
quiz.mistake: Halves the number, or confuses cube root with square root

quiz.q: Joseph builds a solid cube that is 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks tall. How many blocks does he use?
quiz.explain: A solid cube of side 5 needs 5 × 5 × 5 = 125 blocks: 5 layers of 25.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one layer (25) or adds 5 + 5 + 5

quiz.q: What is the smallest number by which 72 must be multiplied to get a perfect cube?
quiz.explain: 72 = (2 × 2 × 2) × 3 × 3. The 3s need one more to make a group of three, so multiply by 3: 72 × 3 = 216 = 6³.
steps: Group of 2s is complete; 3s have only two
quiz.mistake: Uses the pairing rule for squares instead of groups of three

quiz.q: Which of these is a perfect cube?
quiz.mistake: Confuses perfect squares like 144 or 441 with perfect cubes

quiz.q: 4³ = 64 is the sum of which consecutive odd numbers?
quiz.explain: 13 + 15 + 17 + 19 = 64. In the pattern, row 4 has four odd numbers starting right after 11.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the cube pattern with the square pattern (1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16)

quiz.q: What is the last digit of 7³?
quiz.explain: 7³ = 343, which ends in 3. Quick way: 7 × 7 = 49 (ends in 9), 9 × 7 = 63 (ends in 3).
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cube ends in the same digit as the number

quiz.q: What is ∛(−27)?
quiz.explain: (−3) × (−3) × (−3) = 9 × (−3) = −27. The cube root of a negative number is negative.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cube root can never be negative

quiz.q: 1729 = 9³ + 10³. Which other pair of cubes also adds up to 1729?
quiz.explain: 1³ + 12³ = 1 + 1728 = 1729. This is why 1729 is called the taxicab (Hardy–Ramanujan) number.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without computing the cubes (2³ + 11³ = 1339)

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: How do I find a cube root like ∛216 with prime factors? Is it the same as square roots?
teach.praise: Groups of three instead of pairs! 216 = (2×2×2)(3×3×3), so ∛216 = 6. Brilliant!
teach.nudge: For square roots we made pairs. How big should the groups be for cube roots?

learn.hook: Fold a sheet of paper in half again and again. After just 10 folds it would have 1024 layers! Doubling grows faster than you think.
points: In 2⁵, 2 is the base and 5 is the exponent (power). 2⁵ = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.
Each paper fold doubles the layers: after n folds there are 2ⁿ layers.
Powers grow very fast: 2¹⁰ = 1024 is much bigger than 10² = 100, even though both use a 2 and a 10.
A negative base with an even exponent gives a positive answer: (−2)⁴ = 16. With an odd exponent it stays negative: (−2)³ = −8.
(−1) to an even power is 1; (−1) to an odd power is −1.

example.q: Write 1,00,000 as a power of 10 and 81 as a power of 3.

learn.reallife: Messages forwarded on phones, a chain of Diwali greetings where each person sends to 2 more, and computer memory sizes (1024 MB) all grow in powers.

quiz.q: Aisha folds a sheet of paper in half 6 times. How many layers does it have now?
quiz.explain: Each fold doubles the layers, so 6 folds give 2⁶ = 64 layers.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 2 × 6 instead of 2 to the power 6

quiz.q: What is the value of (−2)⁴?
quiz.explain: (−2) × (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = 4 × 4 = 16. Four negative signs pair up to make a positive answer.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the negative sign even though the exponent is even

quiz.q: Which is greater, 2¹⁰ or 10²?
quiz.explain: 2¹⁰ = 1024 and 10² = 100. Swapping base and exponent changes the value a lot.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger base always means a bigger value

quiz.q: Riya writes 81 as a power of 3. What is the exponent?
quiz.explain: 81 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 3⁴, so the exponent is 4.
quiz.mistake: Divides 81 by 3 instead of counting how many 3s multiply to 81

quiz.q: What is (−1)¹⁰¹?
quiz.explain: 101 is odd, so one −1 is left without a partner. (−1) to an odd power is −1.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the base by the exponent

quiz.q: A farmer puts 1 grain on day 1 and doubles the grains every day. How many grains does he put on day 11?
quiz.explain: Day 1 has 2⁰ = 1 grain, day 2 has 2¹, so day 11 has 2¹⁰ = 1024 grains.
quiz.mistake: Uses 2¹¹ and forgets that day 1 starts at 1 grain

quiz.q: How can 64 be written as a power of 4?
quiz.mistake: Divides 64 by 4 to get 16 and uses that as the exponent

quiz.q: In the Indian system, what is 10⁶ called?
quiz.explain: 10⁶ = 10,00,000, which is ten lakh (one million). 1 lakh is 10⁵ and 1 crore is 10⁷.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the place names lakh and crore

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: What does 2⁵ mean? Isn't it just 2 × 5 = 10?
teach.praise: Oh! It is 2 multiplied by itself 5 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32, not 10. Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many times is 2 written down when we work out 2⁵? And what is the answer?

learn.hook: Can you work out 2²⁰ ÷ 2¹⁸ in one second? With the laws of exponents, you can: it is just 2² = 4!
points: Same base, multiply → add the exponents: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ. So 3² × 3⁴ = 3⁶.
Same base, divide → subtract the exponents: aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ. So 7⁹ ÷ 7⁴ = 7⁵.
Power of a power → multiply the exponents: (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ. So (5²)³ = 5⁶.
Same exponent: aᵐ × bᵐ = (ab)ᵐ. So 2³ × 5³ = 10³ = 1000.
Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, and a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ. So 9⁰ = 1 and 2⁻³ = 1/8.

example.q: Simplify (2⁵ × 2³) ÷ 2⁶.

learn.reallife: Scientists and computer engineers use these laws every day, for example to say that 2¹⁰ × 2¹⁰ bytes is 2²⁰ bytes (about one million).

items.text: 2³ × 2⁴ = 2 to the power ___
(5²)³ = 5 to the power ___
7⁹ ÷ 7⁴ = 7 to the power ___

games.title: Law or flaw?
items: Keep the base and add the exponents: 3² × 3³ = 3⁵ = 243.
a⁰ = 1 for every non-zero number a
aⁿ ÷ aⁿ = aⁿ⁻ⁿ = a⁰, and any non-zero number divided by itself is 1.
Power of a power: multiply the exponents, 3 × 2 = 6.
A negative exponent means the reciprocal: 5⁻¹ = 1/5¹.

quiz.q: Simplify 3⁴ × 3².
quiz.explain: Same base, multiplying: add the exponents. 4 + 2 = 6, so the answer is 3⁶.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the exponents or multiplies the bases

quiz.q: What is the value of (2⁵ × 2³) ÷ 2⁶?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts before adding, or stops at 2⁸ = 256

quiz.q: When (4²)³ is written as a single power of 4, what is the exponent?
quiz.explain: Power of a power: multiply the exponents. 2 × 3 = 6, so (4²)³ = 4⁶.
quiz.mistake: Adds the exponents (2 + 3 = 5) instead of multiplying

quiz.q: What is 2025⁰?
quiz.explain: Any non-zero number raised to the power 0 equals 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a power of 0 makes the number 0

quiz.q: What is 5⁻²?
quiz.explain: A negative exponent means the reciprocal: 5⁻² = 1/5² = 1/25.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative exponent makes the answer negative

quiz.q: What is 2³ × 5³?
quiz.explain: Same exponent: 2³ × 5³ = (2 × 5)³ = 10³ = 1000. Check: 8 × 125 = 1000.
quiz.mistake: Adds the exponents to get 10⁶ or multiplies 2 × 5 × 3

quiz.q: Kabir says 2³ × 3² = 6⁵. What is the correct value of 2³ × 3²?
quiz.explain: The bases are different and so are the exponents, so no law joins them. Just calculate: 8 × 9 = 72.
quiz.mistake: Adds exponents even though the bases are different

quiz.q: Which of these is equal to 1/8?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a negative exponent gives a negative number

teach.ask: Gappu scratches his feathers: How do I quickly simplify 3⁴ × 3²? Do I multiply the 4 and the 2?
teach.praise: Keep the same base and add the powers: 3⁴ × 3² = 3⁶. Now I can do it fast!
teach.nudge: When the bases are the same and we multiply, what do we do with the exponents — add or multiply?

learn.hook: The Sun is about 15,00,00,000 km away. Counting those zeros is tiring! Scientists simply write 1.5 × 10⁸ km.
points: Scientific notation (standard form) writes a number as a × 10ⁿ, where a is at least 1 and less than 10.
For a big number, move the decimal point left and count the jumps: 4,50,000 = 4.5 × 10⁵.
For a tiny number, move the decimal point right; the exponent becomes negative: 0.0005 = 5 × 10⁻⁴.
To compare two numbers in standard form, compare the powers of 10 first: 2 × 10⁸ is bigger than 9 × 10⁷.
In the Indian system, 1 lakh = 10⁵ and 1 crore = 10⁷.

example.q: The Moon is about 3,84,000 km from the Earth. Write this in scientific notation.
steps: Put the decimal after the first digit: 3.84
Count how many places the point moved: 5

learn.reallife: India's population (about 1.4 × 10⁹), distances to stars and the size of a virus are all written in scientific notation.

quiz.q: How is 5,60,000 written in scientific notation?
quiz.explain: Move the decimal point 5 places left: 5,60,000 = 5.6 × 10⁵. The first part must be between 1 and 10.
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of zeros (4) instead of the jumps of the decimal point

quiz.q: How is 0.00034 written in scientific notation?
quiz.explain: Move the decimal point 4 places right to get 3.4, so the exponent is −4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the negative sign or miscounts the jumps

quiz.q: What is 2.5 × 10³ in usual form?
quiz.explain: Multiplying by 10³ moves the decimal point 3 places right: 2.5 → 2500.
quiz.mistake: Adds three zeros after 25 to get 25000

quiz.q: 1 crore is 10 raised to what power?
quiz.explain: 1 crore = 1,00,00,000, which has 7 zeros, so it is 10⁷.
quiz.mistake: Confuses crore with 10 lakh (10⁶)

quiz.q: Which is larger: 3 × 10⁸ or 9 × 10⁷?
quiz.explain: 3 × 10⁸ = 30 crore and 9 × 10⁷ = 9 crore. Compare the powers of 10 first.
quiz.mistake: Compares only the front numbers (9 > 3)

quiz.q: Light travels about 3 × 10⁸ m in one second. About how far does it travel in 2 seconds?
quiz.explain: Double the distance: 2 × 3 × 10⁸ = 6 × 10⁸ m. The power of 10 does not change.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the exponent as well as the number

quiz.q: A tiny bacterium is about 0.000002 m long. What is this in scientific notation?
quiz.explain: Move the point 6 places right to get 2, so the length is 2 × 10⁻⁶ m.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the zeros after the decimal point (5)

quiz.explain: Multiply the numbers (2 × 4 = 8) and add the exponents of 10 (3 + 2 = 5): 8 × 10⁵.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the exponents instead of adding them

teach.ask: Gappu blinks: How do I write 4,50,000 in scientific notation? There are so many zeros!
teach.praise: Move the decimal point to get 4.5, count 5 jumps, so 4.5 × 10⁵. Neat and short!
teach.nudge: Where should the decimal point go, and how do you know which power of 10 to use?

topics.title: Counting long ago: tallies, Egyptian and Roman numerals

learn.hook: Long before anyone wrote the digit 7, a shepherd tied a knot in a rope or scratched a mark on a bone for every sheep that went out to graze.
points: The first counting was one-to-one matching: one pebble, knot or tally mark for each object.
Grouping makes counting faster. Tally marks are bundled in fives, so 3 bundles and 2 marks means 17.
Egyptian numerals used a picture for each power of ten: a stroke for 1, a heel bone for 10, a coiled rope for 100 and a lotus flower for 1000. You repeat the pictures and add.
Roman numerals use I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1000. A smaller symbol written before a bigger one is subtracted: IV = 4, XL = 40, XC = 90, CM = 900.
These systems have no place value and no zero, so big numbers need many symbols and sums like 347 × 26 become very hard.

example.q: Write 1984 in Roman numerals.

learn.reallife: Clock towers, chapter numbers in old books and 'Class VIII' written on your notebook all use Roman numerals.

games.title: Ancient number facts
items: I before X is subtracted: IX = 10 − 1 = 9. Eleven is XI.
The Roman system has a symbol for zero.
Roman numerals have no zero at all.
In Egyptian numerals, changing the order of the symbols does not change the value.
Egyptian values are simply added, so order does not matter.
The Egyptian lotus flower stands for 1000.
Stroke = 1, heel bone = 10, coiled rope = 100, lotus = 1000.
The bigger symbol comes first, so add: C + L = 100 + 50 = 150.
XXXX is the standard Roman way to write 40.
Forty is written XL, which means 50 − 10.

quiz.q: What number is MCMXLVII?
quiz.explain: M = 1000, CM = 900, XL = 40 and VII = 7. Together that is 1947, the year India became independent.
quiz.mistake: Adds C and M (1100) instead of subtracting C from M

quiz.q: How is 49 written in Roman numerals?
quiz.explain: 49 = 40 + 9. Forty is XL and nine is IX, so 49 = XLIX.
quiz.mistake: Writes IL by subtracting 1 from 50 in one jump, which the standard rules do not allow

quiz.q: An Egyptian scribe draws 3 lotus flowers, 2 coiled ropes, 4 heel bones and 5 strokes. What number is this?
quiz.explain: Lotus = 1000, rope = 100, heel bone = 10, stroke = 1. So 3000 + 200 + 40 + 5 = 3245.
quiz.mistake: Just counts the pictures (14) or mixes up which picture means what

quiz.q: How many Egyptian symbols are needed to write 999?
quiz.explain: There is no place value, so 999 needs 9 coiled ropes, 9 heel bones and 9 strokes: 27 symbols.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Egyptian numerals use one symbol per digit like our system

quiz.q: Kabir's cricket scorecard shows three bundles of five tally marks and 3 single marks. How many runs is that?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5 runs, so 3 bundles = 15. Add the 3 single marks: 15 + 3 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1 mark instead of 5

quiz.q: Why is it hard to multiply big numbers using Roman numerals?
options: Roman numerals cannot show numbers above 1000
Roman numerals cannot show even numbers
There is no place value or zero, so digits cannot be lined up in columns
Letters are not allowed in maths
quiz.explain: Our column method works because each place has a fixed value. Roman numerals have no place value and no zero, so there are no columns to line up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the problem is the size of numbers rather than the missing place value

quiz.q: Which of these Roman numerals has the largest value?
quiz.explain: DC = 500 + 100 = 600, CD = 500 − 100 = 400, CX = 110 and XC = 90. So DC is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a smaller symbol in front means subtract

quiz.q: Riya sees 'Chapter XIX' in an old storybook. Which chapter is it?
quiz.explain: X = 10 and IX = 9, so XIX = 10 + 9 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Adds every symbol (10 + 1 + 10 = 21) instead of subtracting the I before X

teach.ask: Gappu grumbles: Why does 888 need so many symbols in Roman numerals (DCCCLXXXVIII) but only three digits in our numbers?
teach.praise: Yes! Roman numerals only add and repeat symbols, but our digits get their value from their place, with zero holding empty places. Clever!
teach.nudge: In 888, do all three 8s mean the same thing? What gives each 8 a different value?

topics.title: Place value and the story of zero

learn.hook: With just ten symbols, 0 to 9, you can write any number you can imagine. The secret? Place value, and a humble little zero.
points: In a place value system, a digit's value depends on its position. In 555 the three 5s mean 500, 50 and 5.
Our system is base 10: each place is worth 10 times the place on its right (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands...).
Zero is a placeholder: 205 and 25 are different numbers because the 0 keeps the tens place empty.
About 4000 years ago the Babylonians used place value with base 60. The Maya of Central America used base 20 and drew a shell for zero.
Indian mathematicians built the base-10 system with zero as a number. Brahmagupta (7th century CE) wrote rules like a + 0 = a and a − a = 0. These numerals travelled through the Arab world to Europe.

example.q: Write 40,305 in expanded form using powers of 10.
steps: Zeros add nothing, but they keep the other digits in their places

learn.reallife: Every price tag, PIN code and cricket score uses place value. One extra zero turns a ₹500 note into ₹5000!

items.text: In 7,382 the value of the digit 3 is ___
Our number system uses base ___
The Babylonians counted in base ___
The Maya counted in base ___
Brahmagupta's rule: a number minus itself equals ___

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 4,60,213?
quiz.explain: Reading the places of 4,60,213 from the left: lakh, ten-thousand, thousand, hundred, ten, one. The 6 is in the ten-thousands place, so it is worth 60,000.
quiz.mistake: Reads the place of the digit wrongly because of the Indian commas

quiz.q: Which number is 3 × 10³ + 5 × 10 + 2?
quiz.explain: 3 × 1000 = 3000, 5 × 10 = 50 and 2 more. 3000 + 50 + 2 = 3052. The hundreds place is empty, so it gets a 0.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the zero in the empty hundreds place

quiz.q: Why does a place value system need a zero?
options: To show an empty place, like the tens place in 405
To make every number look bigger
To stand for the number ten
quiz.explain: Without 0, 405 and 45 would look the same. Zero holds an empty place so the other digits stay in the right positions.
quiz.mistake: Thinks zero is just 'nothing' and has no job to do

quiz.q: The Babylonians counted in base 60. A number shows 2 in the 'sixties' place and 5 in the ones place. What is it in our numbers?
quiz.explain: 2 sixties and 5 ones = 2 × 60 + 5 = 125. It is just like 2 minutes 5 seconds = 125 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits as if they were in base 10

quiz.q: Which Indian mathematician wrote rules for working with zero, such as a − a = 0, in the 7th century CE?
quiz.explain: Brahmagupta wrote rules for adding, subtracting and multiplying with zero in 628 CE, treating zero as a number.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Indian mathematicians with Greek ones

quiz.q: The Maya counted in base 20. A Maya number has 3 in the 'twenties' place and 4 in the ones place. What is it in our numbers?
quiz.explain: 3 twenties and 4 ones = 3 × 20 + 4 = 64.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits as base 10 and gets 34

quiz.q: We still use the Babylonian base 60 for time. How many seconds are there in 1 hour?
quiz.explain: 1 hour = 60 minutes and each minute has 60 seconds, so 60 × 60 = 3600 seconds.
quiz.mistake: Adds 60 + 60 or multiplies by 10 instead of 60

quiz.q: Meena writes 'five thousand and seven' as 57. What did she forget?
options: Zeros to hold the empty hundreds and tens places
That place value works only for small numbers
quiz.explain: Five thousand and seven is 5007. The hundreds and tens places are empty, so they need zeros.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that empty places must be filled with zero

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: 205 and 25 use the same digits 2 and 5. Why are they different numbers?
teach.praise: I see! In 205 the 0 holds the tens place empty, so the 2 moves to the hundreds place. Place value is powerful!
teach.nudge: Where does the 2 sit in 205, and where does it sit in 25? What is the 0 doing?

learn.hook: Computers count with only two digits, 0 and 1. To a computer, 1010 means ten!
points: The base tells how many make one group before you move to the next place. Base 10 groups in tens, base 5 in fives and base 2 in twos.
In base 2 (binary) the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ... So 1011 in base 2 = 8 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 11.
In base 5 the place values are 1, 5, 25, 125, ... and only the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 are used.
To write a number in base 2, break it into place values: 13 = 8 + 4 + 1, so 13 = 1101 in base 2.
Base 10 probably comes from our ten fingers, and base 60 still lives on in hours, minutes and seconds.

example.q: Write 13 in base 2.

learn.reallife: Every photo, song and game on a phone is stored as long strings of 0s and 1s. That is binary, base 2.

quiz.q: What is 1101 (base 2) in our base 10?
quiz.explain: The places are 8, 4, 2, 1. 1101 means 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Just adds the digits (3) or reads it as a base-10 number

quiz.q: How is 6 written in base 2?
quiz.explain: 6 = 4 + 2. Places 4, 2, 1 get 1, 1, 0, so 6 = 110 in base 2.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the wrong order or uses the place values wrongly

quiz.q: Which digits are used in base 5?
quiz.explain: In base 5, as soon as you reach 5 you make a new group, so only 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 are needed.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the base number itself is one of the digits

quiz.q: What is 32 (base 5) in base 10?
quiz.explain: 3 fives and 2 ones: 3 × 5 + 2 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Reads the number as base 10, or swaps the digits (2 × 5 + 3 = 13)

quiz.q: What are the first four place values in base 2, starting from the right?
quiz.explain: Each place is 2 times the one on its right: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, ...
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 each time instead of multiplying by 2

quiz.q: Harpreet packs 19 laddoos in boxes of 5. How is 19 written in base 5?
quiz.explain: 19 = 3 boxes of 5 + 4 loose laddoos, so 19 = 34 in base 5. Check: 3 × 5 + 4 = 19.
quiz.mistake: Writes the remainder first, or uses the digit 9 which base 5 does not have

quiz.q: A movie lasts 150 minutes. How many hours and minutes is that?
quiz.explain: 150 = 2 × 60 + 30, so it is 2 hours and 30 minutes. Time works in base 60, not base 100.
quiz.mistake: Treats an hour as 100 minutes and reads 150 as 1 hour 50 minutes

quiz.q: What is the largest number (in base 10) that can be written using only 4 digits in base 2?
quiz.explain: The largest 4-digit binary number is 1111 = 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15. The next number, 16, needs 5 digits (10000).
quiz.mistake: Thinks 2⁴ = 16 itself fits in 4 binary digits

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can a computer write the number 5 if it only knows 0 and 1?
teach.praise: Wow, 5 = 4 + 1, so in binary it is 101. Places go 1, 2, 4, 8! Computers are smart and so are you!
teach.nudge: What are the place values in base 2? Which of them add up to 5?

learn.hook: The blackboard, your maths notebook, a door, and the paper kite you fly on Makar Sankranti are all quadrilaterals. But they are not all the same kind!
points: A quadrilateral is a closed figure with 4 straight sides, 4 vertices, 4 angles and 2 diagonals.
A trapezium has a pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A rectangle is a parallelogram with all four angles 90°. A rhombus is a parallelogram with all four sides equal.
A square has all sides equal and all angles 90°, so every square is a rectangle and also a rhombus.
A kite has two pairs of equal sides, and each pair sits next to each other (adjacent).

example.q: A quadrilateral has all four sides 5 cm, and one of its angles is 90°. Which quadrilateral is it?
steps: All sides equal, so it is a rhombus, which is a parallelogram
In a parallelogram, opposite angles are equal and neighbouring angles add to 180°
So one 90° angle makes all four angles 90°
All sides equal and all angles 90° means a square

learn.reallife: Carpenters check that a door frame is a true rectangle, and rangoli makers love rhombus and kite patterns.

games.title: Name that quadrilateral
pairs: only one pair of parallel sides

games.title: Family of shapes
items: A square has four right angles and opposite sides equal, so it is a special rectangle.
A 4 cm by 7 cm rectangle does not have all sides equal.
A rhombus has both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A kite always has 4 equal sides.
A kite needs only two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, like 3, 3, 5, 5.
A square has all four sides equal.

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral has all four sides equal and all four angles equal to 90°?
quiz.explain: A square has equal sides like a rhombus and right angles like a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Picks rhombus, forgetting that a rhombus need not have right angles

quiz.q: How many diagonals does a quadrilateral have?
quiz.explain: Each vertex joins only the opposite vertex by a diagonal. That gives 2 diagonals, like AC and BD.
steps: From A: only AC is a diagonal
AC and BD are counted once each: 2
quiz.mistake: Counts each diagonal twice or confuses diagonals with sides

quiz.q: Arjun's paper kite has sides 30 cm, 30 cm, 45 cm and 45 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Perimeter is the sum of all four sides: 30 + 30 + 45 + 45 = 150 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides (75 cm)

quiz.q: A quadrilateral has opposite sides parallel and all angles 90°. Its neighbouring sides are 4 cm and 7 cm. What is it?
quiz.explain: Four right angles with unequal neighbouring sides make a rectangle, not a square.
quiz.mistake: Calls every shape with right angles a square

quiz.q: Which statement is true?
quiz.explain: A square has all four sides equal, so it is always a rhombus. A rhombus need not have right angles, so it is not always a square.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the 'special case' relationship between square and rhombus

quiz.q: One side of a rhombus is 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: All four sides of a rhombus are equal, so the perimeter is 4 × 6 = 24 cm.
quiz.mistake: Uses only two sides, or squares the side (36)

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral can have exactly one pair of parallel sides?
quiz.explain: Parallelograms, rhombuses and rectangles always have two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezium can have just one pair.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rhombus or rectangle has only one pair of parallel sides

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80°, 95° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 80 + 95 + 110 = 285, and 360 − 285 = 75°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° (the triangle angle sum) or makes an adding slip

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: My friend says a square is a rectangle. That sounds wrong! Is it?
teach.praise: Yes! A square has four right angles and equal opposite sides, so it is a special kind of rectangle. Thanks!
teach.nudge: What does a shape need to be a rectangle? Does a square have those things?

learn.hook: Push a rectangular photo frame from one corner and it leans over, but its opposite sides stay parallel. You have made a parallelogram!
points: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are equal and parallel.
Opposite angles are equal.
Neighbouring (adjacent) angles add up to 180°.
The diagonals bisect each other: they cut each other exactly in half. They are not always equal.
Why? A diagonal splits a parallelogram into two identical (congruent) triangles.

example.q: In parallelogram PQRS, ∠P = 70°. Find ∠Q, ∠R and ∠S.

learn.reallife: Folding stools, car jacks and the scissor-lift used to fix street lights all use parallelograms that change shape but keep opposite sides parallel.

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 65°. What is ∠C?
quiz.explain: ∠A and ∠C are opposite angles, and opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks opposite angles add to 180° instead of being equal

quiz.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 65°. What is ∠B?
quiz.explain: ∠A and ∠B are neighbouring angles, so they add up to 180°. ∠B = 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all angles of a parallelogram are equal, or subtracts from 90°

quiz.q: The diagonals of parallelogram PQRS meet at O. If PR = 16 cm, how long is PO?
quiz.explain: The diagonals bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of PR. PO = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.
steps: O is the midpoint of PR
quiz.mistake: Forgets that the diagonals cut each other in half

quiz.q: Two neighbouring angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the smaller angle?
quiz.explain: Neighbouring angles add to 180°. Split 180° in the ratio 2 : 3: 180 ÷ 5 = 36, so the angles are 72° and 108°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 360° instead of 180° for neighbouring angles (gets 144°)

quiz.q: Joseph's garden gate is a parallelogram with sides 120 cm and 80 cm. What is its perimeter?
quiz.explain: Opposite sides are equal, so the perimeter is 2 × (120 + 80) = 400 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two sides, or multiplies the sides like an area

quiz.q: Which property is NOT always true for a parallelogram?
quiz.explain: In a leaning parallelogram one diagonal is clearly longer than the other. Equal diagonals happen only when it is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'diagonals bisect each other' with 'diagonals are equal'

quiz.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 90°. What can you say about its other angles?
quiz.explain: The opposite angle is also 90°, and each neighbouring angle is 180° − 90° = 90°. So all four are right angles: it is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that neighbouring angles must add up to 180°

quiz.q: Two neighbouring angles of a parallelogram are (x + 20)° and (2x + 10)°. What is x?
quiz.explain: Neighbouring angles add to 180°: 3x + 30 = 180, so 3x = 150 and x = 50. The angles are 70° and 110°.
quiz.mistake: Sets the two angles equal to each other instead of adding them to 180°

teach.ask: Gappu asks: In a parallelogram, if I know one angle is 70°, how can I find all the other angles?
teach.praise: Opposite angles are equal and neighbouring ones add to 180°, so 70°, 110°, 70°, 110°. Super!
teach.nudge: What do you know about the angle opposite to 70°? And about the angles next to it?

learn.hook: Draw any quadrilateral at all, even a wonky one. Tear off its four corners and put them together: they always make a full turn of 360°!
points: The angles of every quadrilateral add up to 360°, because a diagonal splits it into two triangles: 180° + 180°.
Rectangle: the diagonals are equal and bisect each other.
Rhombus: the diagonals bisect each other at right angles (they are perpendicular), and each diagonal bisects the angles at its ends.
Square: the diagonals are equal, perpendicular and bisect each other. It has every property of a rectangle and a rhombus.
Kite: the diagonals are perpendicular, and one diagonal cuts the other in half.

example.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. Find each angle.

learn.reallife: Tile makers and architects use the 360° rule to check that floor tiles and window frames fit together with no gaps.

games.title: Always true for a rectangle?
buckets: Not always true for a rectangle

games.title: From general to special
games.prompt: Each shape is a special kind of the one before it. Start with the most general.

quiz.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 90°, 90° and 120°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: The four angles add up to 360°. 90 + 90 + 120 = 300, so the fourth angle is 360 − 300 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Assumes the missing angle must also be 90°

quiz.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: 10x = 360°, so x = 36° and the largest angle is 4x = 144°.
quiz.mistake: Stops at x = 36° and forgets to find 4x

quiz.q: In rectangle ABCD, diagonal AC is 13 cm. How long is diagonal BD?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a rectangle are equal, so BD = AC = 13 cm.
quiz.mistake: Halves the diagonal, mixing up 'equal' with 'bisect each other'

quiz.q: At what angle do the diagonals of a rhombus cross each other?
quiz.explain: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular, so they always cross at 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the angle depends on the side length

quiz.q: Which quadrilateral always has diagonals that are equal AND perpendicular?
quiz.explain: A rectangle has equal diagonals and a rhombus has perpendicular ones. Only a square always has both.
quiz.mistake: Remembers only one of the two diagonal properties

quiz.q: Why do the angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°?
options: It always has four right angles
A diagonal splits it into two triangles, and 180° + 180° = 360°
Every quadrilateral fits exactly inside a circle
Its four sides add up to 360
quiz.explain: Each triangle has an angle sum of 180°. A diagonal cuts any quadrilateral into two triangles, so the total is 360°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rule only works because squares have four 90° angles

quiz.q: In rhombus PQRS, ∠P = 120°. The diagonal PR bisects ∠P. What angle does PR make with side PQ?
quiz.explain: A diagonal of a rhombus bisects the angle at its end, so it splits 120° into two angles of 60°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'bisects the angle' with 'is perpendicular'

quiz.q: Aisha draws a quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles but are NOT equal. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: Diagonals that bisect each other at 90° make a rhombus. Since they are not equal, it cannot be a square.
quiz.mistake: Picks kite, but in a kite only one diagonal is cut in half

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: My quadrilateral is all crooked. How can its angles still add up to 360°?
teach.praise: Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles, each with 180°, so 360° in total. It works for any shape!
teach.nudge: What happens if you draw a line from one corner to the opposite corner? What shapes do you get?

learn.hook: Can you tell whether 7,35,816 is divisible by 8 without dividing at all? Just peek at the last three digits!
points: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even, by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5, and by 10 if it ends in 0.
Divisible by 4: check the number made by the last two digits. This works because 100 is a multiple of 4.
Divisible by 8: check the number made by the last three digits. This works because 1000 = 8 × 125.
A number divisible by 8 is also divisible by 4 and 2, but a number divisible by 4 need not be divisible by 8 (like 12).
The remainder on dividing by 4 is the same as the remainder for the last two digits: 9,147 → 47 → remainder 3.

example.q: Is 73,512 divisible by 8? Is it divisible by 4?
steps: Every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4
example.answer: Yes, it is divisible by both 8 and 4

learn.reallife: Leap years use the rule for 4: the year 2028 is a leap year because 28 is divisible by 4.

games.title: Divisibility detective
items: If a number is divisible by 4, it is divisible by 8.
12 is divisible by 4 but not by 8.
If a number is divisible by 8, it is divisible by 4.
8 = 4 × 2, so every multiple of 8 is a multiple of 4.
Its last three digits are 000, and 0 is divisible by 8.
A number ending in 5 can be even.
The last two digits make 30, and 30 is not a multiple of 4.
Every number divisible by 10 is divisible by both 2 and 5.
10 = 2 × 5, so any multiple of 10 is a multiple of 2 and of 5.

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 4?
quiz.explain: Look at the last two digits: 18, 22, 36 and 10. Only 36 is a multiple of 4 (4 × 9), so 7,236 is divisible by 4.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every even number is divisible by 4

quiz.q: What is the smallest digit that can fill the blank in 52_4 to make it divisible by 8?
quiz.explain: Check the last three digits 2_4. 204 and 214 are not multiples of 8, but 224 = 8 × 28. So the smallest digit is 2.
quiz.mistake: Picks 0 without checking, or looks only at the last two digits

quiz.q: Kabir checks whether 1,236 is divisible by 4. Which reasoning is correct?
options: No, because 6 is not divisible by 4
Yes, because its last two digits make 36, which is divisible by 4
Yes, because its digits add up to 12
quiz.explain: The test for 4 uses the number made by the last two digits. 36 = 4 × 9, so 1,236 is divisible by 4.
quiz.mistake: Uses only the last digit, or uses the digit-sum test that belongs to 3 and 9

quiz.q: How many numbers from 1 to 100 are divisible by 4?
quiz.explain: The multiples of 4 up to 100 are 4, 8, ..., 100. That is 100 ÷ 4 = 25 numbers.
steps: Largest multiple of 4 up to 100 is 100 = 4 × 25
quiz.mistake: Leaves out 100 itself, or counts even numbers instead

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 8?
quiz.explain: Check the last three digits: 108, 324, 220 and 416. Only 416 = 8 × 52 is a multiple of 8.
quiz.mistake: Checks only the last two digits, which is the test for 4

quiz.q: Why does the test for 4 only look at the last two digits?
options: Because 100 is a multiple of 4, so the hundreds and higher places never leave a remainder
Because the last two digits are always the largest
It is just a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: Any number = (hundreds part) + (last two digits). The hundreds part is a multiple of 100 = 4 × 25, so only the last two digits decide.
quiz.mistake: Believes divisibility rules are magic instead of place value

quiz.q: Riya's number is divisible by both 2 and 5. What must its last digit be?
quiz.explain: Divisible by 5 means it ends in 0 or 5. Divisible by 2 means it is even. Only 0 does both.
quiz.mistake: Picks 5, forgetting the number must also be even

quiz.q: What is the remainder when 9,147 is divided by 4?
quiz.explain: The remainder is the same as for the last two digits, 47. 47 = 4 × 11 + 3, so the remainder is 3.
quiz.mistake: Uses only the last digit (7) as the remainder

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I check if 5,732 is divisible by 4 without long division?
teach.praise: The last two digits make 32 = 4 × 8, and 100 is a multiple of 4 anyway. So yes! Easy peasy!
teach.nudge: Which part of the number do you need to look at for 4? Why can we ignore the rest?

learn.hook: Add the digits of 61,875: 6 + 1 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 27. Because 27 is a multiple of 9, so is 61,875. Magic? No, place value!
points: A number is divisible by 3 if its digit sum is divisible by 3, and divisible by 9 if its digit sum is divisible by 9.
Why it works: 10 = 9 + 1, 100 = 99 + 1, 1000 = 999 + 1. So a number and its digit sum leave the same remainder when divided by 9 (or by 3).
Digital root: keep adding the digits until one digit is left. For 9,875: 29 → 11 → 2, so 9,875 leaves remainder 2 when divided by 9.
Divisible by 6: the number must be divisible by both 2 and 3.
Divisible by 11: starting from the right, subtract and add the digits in turn. If the result is 0 or a multiple of 11, so is the number.

example.q: Is 61,875 divisible by 9? Is it divisible by 6?
steps: 61,875 is odd, so it is not divisible by 2
So it is not divisible by 6

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers use digit sums to quickly check bills: if the digital roots do not match, there is a mistake somewhere.

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 9?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a number ending in 8 or 9 must be divisible by 9

quiz.q: What is the digital root of 58,463?
quiz.explain: 5 + 8 + 4 + 6 + 3 = 26, and 2 + 6 = 8. The digital root is 8.
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first digit sum (26)

quiz.q: What is the remainder when 1,234 is divided by 9?
quiz.explain: The digit sum is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, and 10 leaves remainder 1 when divided by 9. Check: 9 × 137 = 1233, and 1234 − 1233 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Uses the last digit as the remainder

quiz.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 11?
quiz.explain: For 9,152, from the right: 2 − 5 + 1 − 9 = −11, a multiple of 11. Indeed 9,152 = 11 × 832.
quiz.mistake: Adds all the digits, which is the test for 3 and 9

quiz.q: Arjun wants 74_5 to be divisible by 3. Which of these digits can fill the blank?
quiz.explain: Digit sum = 7 + 4 + _ + 5 = 16 + _. With 2 it becomes 18, a multiple of 3. With 3, 4 or 6 it becomes 19, 20 or 22.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to include the fixed digits in the digit sum

quiz.q: Is 2,346 divisible by 6?
options: No, because its digit sum 15 is not divisible by 6
Yes, because it is even and its digit sum 15 is divisible by 3
Yes, only because its last digit is 6
No, because it is not divisible by 3
quiz.explain: 6 = 2 × 3. 2,346 is even, and 2 + 3 + 4 + 6 = 15 is divisible by 3, so 2,346 is divisible by 6 (2,346 = 6 × 391).
quiz.mistake: Thinks the digit sum must be divisible by 6

quiz.q: Meena says: every number divisible by 3 is also divisible by 9. Which number proves her wrong?
quiz.explain: 12 = 3 × 4 is divisible by 3, but 12 ÷ 9 is not a whole number. The other three are all multiples of 9.
quiz.mistake: Picks a multiple of 9, which agrees with Meena instead of proving her wrong

quiz.q: Why does the digit-sum test work for 9?
options: Because 10, 100, 1000, ... are each 1 more than a multiple of 9
quiz.explain: Each 1 ten, 1 hundred or 1 thousand is a multiple of 9 plus 1. So each digit adds just itself to the remainder, and the digit sum gives the same remainder.
quiz.mistake: Links the rule to 9 being a big digit instead of to place value

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I find out whether 4,518 is divisible by 9 without dividing?
teach.praise: Add the digits: 4 + 5 + 1 + 8 = 18, a multiple of 9, so 4,518 is too. That is a cool shortcut!
teach.nudge: What should you do with the digits 4, 5, 1 and 8? Then what do you check?

learn.hook: Pick any 2-digit number, reverse its digits and subtract the smaller from the larger. Your friend can bet the answer is in the 9 times table, every single time!
points: Parity means odd or even. Even + even = even, odd + odd = even, odd + even = odd, odd × odd = odd.
The sum of any 3 consecutive numbers is 3 times the middle one: (n − 1) + n + (n + 1) = 3n.
Triangular numbers 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, ... are sums 1 + 2 + ... + n, and equal n(n + 1) ÷ 2.
The reverse-and-subtract trick: (10a + b) − (10b + a) = 9(a − b), so the answer is always a multiple of 9.
In a cryptarithm, letters stand for digits. Use carries, last digits and parity to crack it.

example.q: In the puzzle A + A + A = BA, each letter is a different digit. Find A and B.
steps: 3 × A ends in the digit A, so 2 × A must end in 0
A = 0 gives 0 + 0 + 0 = 0, which is not a 2-digit number

learn.reallife: Puzzle pages in newspapers, Sudoku and magic tricks at a Diwali party all use these number patterns.

items.q: 3 consecutive numbers add to 45. Middle one?

quiz.q: Three consecutive numbers add up to 72. What is the largest of them?
quiz.explain: The sum is 3 times the middle number, so the middle is 72 ÷ 3 = 24. The numbers are 23, 24, 25, so the largest is 25.
quiz.mistake: Gives the middle number instead of the largest

quiz.q: Is the sum of 13 odd numbers odd or even?
options: It depends on which odd numbers
quiz.explain: Two odd numbers make an even sum. 13 odd numbers make 6 pairs (even) plus one odd number left over, so the total is odd.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding odd numbers always gives an even answer

quiz.q: Harpreet adds all the numbers from 1 to 50. What total does she get?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to divide by 2 (gets 2550)

quiz.q: Joseph takes any 2-digit number, reverses its digits and subtracts the smaller from the larger. The answer is always a multiple of which number?
quiz.explain: (10a + b) − (10b + a) = 9a − 9b = 9(a − b). For example, 41 − 14 = 27 = 9 × 3, which is not a multiple of 2, 4 or 5.
quiz.mistake: Generalises from one example such as 82 − 28 = 54, which is also even

quiz.q: In the sum 4A + A4 = 99, A stands for one digit. What is A?
quiz.explain: 4A means 40 + A and A4 means 10A + 4. So 44 + 11A = 99, giving 11A = 55 and A = 5. Check: 45 + 54 = 99.
quiz.mistake: Treats 4A as 4 × A instead of a 2-digit number

quiz.q: Is (odd × even) + odd always odd or always even?
quiz.explain: Odd × even is even. Then even + odd is odd. For example, 3 × 4 + 5 = 17.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying by an odd number keeps a number odd

quiz.q: The 7th triangular number is 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7. What is it?
quiz.explain: 7 × 8 ÷ 2 = 28. You can stack 28 dots into a triangle with rows of 1, 2, ..., 7.
quiz.mistake: Gives the 6th triangular number (21) or the square 7² = 49

quiz.q: Aisha says the sum of any 4 consecutive numbers is a multiple of 4. She tests 1 + 2 + 3 + 4. What does she find?
options: The sum is 10, so she is right
The sum is 10, so she is wrong
The sum is 12, so she is right
The sum is 8, so she is right
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, and 10 is not a multiple of 4. One counter-example is enough to show the claim is false.
quiz.mistake: Mixes this up with the true rule for 3 consecutive numbers

teach.ask: Gappu asks: Why is the sum of three numbers in a row, like 7 + 8 + 9, always in the 3 times table?
teach.praise: The first is one less and the last is one more than the middle, so they balance out. 3 times the middle! Brilliant!
teach.nudge: Compare the first and last numbers with the middle one. What happens when you add them?

learn.hook: Can you work out 7 × 102 in your head in two seconds? Split 102 into 100 + 2, and it is 700 + 14 = 714!
points: Distributive property: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. For example, 6 × 47 = 6 × 40 + 6 × 7 = 240 + 42 = 282.
It works with subtraction too: a × (b − c) = a × b − a × c. So 8 × 99 = 800 − 8 = 792.
Area picture: a rectangle a wide and (b + c) long splits into two rectangles with areas ab and ac.
Two brackets: (a + b)(c + d) = ac + ad + bc + bd. Every term in the first bracket multiplies every term in the second.
It works for algebra: 3x(2x + 5) = 6x² + 15x.

example.q: Find 23 × 14 by splitting both numbers.

learn.reallife: A shopkeeper selling 6 kurtas at ₹499 each thinks 6 × 500 − 6 × 1 = ₹3000 − ₹6 = ₹2994. Quick and correct!

quiz.q: Simplify 5(2x + 3).
quiz.explain: Multiply 5 with each term inside: 5 × 2x = 10x and 5 × 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the first term inside the bracket

quiz.q: What is 8 × 99, using the distributive property?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Expand (x + 3)(x + 4).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only first × first and last × last, missing the middle terms

quiz.q: Riya buys 6 pens at ₹47 each. She works it out as 6 × 40 + 6 × 7. How much does she pay?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the tens part by 6 and adds 7

quiz.q: Expand 3a(a − 2b).
quiz.explain: 3a × a = 3a² and 3a × 2b = 6ab, keeping the minus sign: 3a² − 6ab.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply the second term by 3a, or loses the minus sign

quiz.q: A garden is 9 m wide and (10 + 2) m long. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 9 by 10 only and then adds 2

quiz.q: Expand (2x + 1)(x − 3).
quiz.mistake: Makes a sign slip when combining −6x and x

quiz.q: When expanding (a + b)(c + d), how many products do you write before combining like terms?
quiz.explain: Each of the 2 terms in the first bracket multiplies each of the 2 terms in the second: 2 × 2 = 4 products (ac, ad, bc, bd).
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only matching terms, giving just 2 products

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I multiply 4 × (x + 3)? Is it 4x + 3?
teach.praise: The 4 must multiply each term inside: 4 × x and 4 × 3, so 4x + 12. Got it!
teach.nudge: Does the 4 multiply only the x, or every term inside the bracket?

learn.hook: Is (a + b)² the same as a² + b²? Try a = 1 and b = 1: (1 + 1)² = 4 but 1² + 1² = 2. Something is missing!
points: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². In a square of side (a + b), there are two a × b rectangles besides the squares a² and b².
(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².
An identity is true for every value of the letters, unlike an equation such as x + 3 = 7, which is true for only one value.

example.q: Find 51² using an identity.

learn.reallife: Builders use (a + b)² when a square courtyard of side a is made b metres longer and b metres wider: the new area is a² + 2ab + b².

games.title: Identity or imposter?
items: (a + b)² = a² + b² for all numbers a and b.
With a = b = 1, the left side is 4 and the right side is 2. The 2ab term is missing.
(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² with a = x, b = 3.
b − a is the negative of a − b, and a number and its negative have the same square.

quiz.q: Expand (x + 6)².
quiz.mistake: Squares each term and forgets the middle term 2ab

quiz.q: Use (a + b)² to find 21².
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 2ab term and gets 401

quiz.q: What is 98²?
quiz.mistake: Writes 100² − 2² (9996), forgetting the middle term

quiz.q: Expand (3y − 2)².
quiz.mistake: Writes 3y² instead of squaring the 3 as well

quiz.q: If a + b = 7 and ab = 10, what is a² + b²?
quiz.explain: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab, so a² + b² = 49 − 20 = 29. (Check: a = 5, b = 2 gives 25 + 4 = 29.)
quiz.mistake: Adds 2ab instead of subtracting it (gets 69)

quiz.q: Kabir's square plot has side (x + 2) m. Which expression gives its area in m²?
quiz.mistake: Writes the perimeter 4x + 8, or forgets the middle term

quiz.q: What is 105²?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 × 5 instead of 2 × 100 × 5 for the middle term (gets 10,525)

quiz.q: Harpreet tests the rule with a = 3 and b = 4. What is (3 + 4)²?
quiz.explain: (3 + 4)² = 7² = 49. Note that 3² + 4² = 25, which is different, so (a + b)² is not a² + b². The missing part is 2ab = 24.
quiz.mistake: Squares each number separately and adds (gets 25)

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: (a + b)² is just a² + b², right? Square both and add!
teach.praise: Oh! The square of side a + b has two a × b rectangles too, so (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b². I was missing a piece!
teach.nudge: Draw a square of side a + b. Besides a² and b², what other pieces are inside it?

topics.title: Difference of squares and quick products

learn.hook: 52 × 48 looks hard, but 52 and 48 are 2 more and 2 less than 50. So it is just 50² − 2² = 2496!
points: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b². The middle terms +ab and −ab cancel out.
Difference of squares the other way: 47² − 43² = (47 + 43)(47 − 43) = 90 × 4 = 360.
Picture: from an a × a square, cut off a b × b corner. The leftover pieces rearrange into a rectangle (a + b) by (a − b).

example.q: Find 103 × 97 quickly.

learn.reallife: Mental-maths champions use (a + b)(a − b) to multiply numbers like 61 × 59 = 3600 − 1 = 3599 in a flash.

quiz.q: What is 41 × 39, using (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²?
quiz.mistake: Adds b² instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Find 47² − 43² without squaring either number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a² − b² = (a − b)², which gives 16

quiz.q: Expand (x + 5)(x − 5).
quiz.explain: This is (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² with a = x and b = 5, so the answer is x² − 25.
quiz.mistake: Gets the sign of 25 wrong

quiz.q: Expand (x + 3)(x + 7).
quiz.explain: (x + a)(x + b) = x² + (a + b)x + ab = x² + 10x + 21.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the sum and the product

quiz.q: Meena's square rangoli has side 25 cm. She cuts a 5 cm square out of one corner. What area is left?
quiz.mistake: Uses (25 − 5)² = 400 instead of 25² − 5²

quiz.q: What is 999 × 1001?
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of subtracting, or rounds to 1000²

quiz.q: Which product equals x² − 9?
quiz.explain: (x + 3)(x − 3) = x² − 3² = x² − 9. (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, which has a middle term.
quiz.mistake: Thinks (x − 3)² equals x² − 9

quiz.q: (x + 4)(x − 2) = x² + px − 8. What is p?
quiz.explain: The x-term is (4 + (−2))x = 2x, so p = 2. Check the constant: 4 × (−2) = −8.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the minus sign and adds 4 + 2 = 6

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I find 52 × 48 in my head? It looks too hard!
teach.praise: 52 and 48 are 50 plus 2 and 50 minus 2, so 50² − 2² = 2500 − 4 = 2496. Wow, magic maths!
teach.nudge: Which number is exactly in the middle of 52 and 48? How far is each number from it?

learn.hook: Nimbu pani tastes perfect with 1 spoon of sugar for every 2 glasses of water. For 6 glasses you need 3 spoons. That is a ratio at work!
points: A ratio a : b compares two quantities of the same kind by division. 12 boys and 18 girls give 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.
Use the same unit before writing a ratio: 50 cm : 2 m = 50 cm : 200 cm = 1 : 4.
Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both terms by the same non-zero number: 2 : 3 = 4 : 6 = 10 : 15.
Order matters: 2 : 3 is not the same as 3 : 2.
Part-to-whole: if boys : girls = 2 : 3, then boys are 2 out of every 5 children, that is 2/5 of the class.

example.q: Write 45 minutes : 2 hours in simplest form.
steps: Change to the same unit: 2 hours = 120 minutes

learn.reallife: Recipes, mixing cement and sand, and the 3 : 2 shape of the Indian flag all use ratios.

games.title: Ratio riddles
items: Order matters. 2 : 3 means the first is smaller; 3 : 2 means the first is bigger.
Change to the same unit first: 100 cm : 50 cm = 2 : 1.
If boys : girls = 3 : 5, then 3/8 of the class are boys.
Out of every 3 + 5 = 8 children, 3 are boys.
Adding the same number to both terms keeps a ratio the same.
1 : 2 becomes 2 : 3 after adding 1, and 1/2 is not equal to 2/3.
Once both quantities are in the same unit, a ratio has no unit.
The units cancel when we divide, e.g. 50 cm ÷ 200 cm = 1/4.

quiz.q: A class has 12 boys and 18 girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 12 : 18. Divide both by their HCF 6 to get 2 : 3.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the order, or does not divide by the HCF fully (6 : 9)

quiz.q: What is the ratio of 50 cm to 2 m?
quiz.explain: Change 2 m to 200 cm. Then 50 : 200 = 1 : 4.
quiz.mistake: Compares the numbers 50 and 2 without changing to the same unit

quiz.q: Arjun cooks rice with 2 cups of rice to 3 cups of water. Which ratio is equivalent to 2 : 3?
quiz.explain: Multiply both terms of 2 : 3 by 4 to get 8 : 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds the same number to both terms (2 + 2 : 3 + 2 = 4 : 5)

quiz.q: In a class of 40, the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. How many girls are there?
quiz.explain: There are 3 + 5 = 8 parts. Each part is 40 ÷ 8 = 5 children, so girls = 5 × 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Finds the number of boys (15) instead of girls

quiz.q: Find x if 4 : 7 = x : 35.
quiz.explain: 7 was multiplied by 5 to get 35, so multiply 4 by 5 too: x = 20.
quiz.mistake: Adds 28 to 4 (because 7 + 28 = 35) instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Write 45 minutes : 1.5 hours in simplest form.
quiz.explain: 1.5 hours = 90 minutes. 45 : 90 = 1 : 2.
quiz.mistake: Mixes units, or reverses the ratio

quiz.q: In a cricket match Harpreet scored 48 runs and Joseph scored 36 runs. What fraction of their total runs did Harpreet score?
quiz.explain: Total = 48 + 36 = 84. Harpreet's share = 48/84 = 4/7.
quiz.mistake: Writes the part-to-part ratio 48/36 = 4/3 instead of part-to-whole

quiz.q: Riya adds 1 to both terms of 1 : 2 and gets 2 : 3. Is the new ratio equivalent to the old one?
options: Yes, adding the same number keeps ratios equal
Yes, because both ratios grew by 1
quiz.explain: Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing, not adding. 1/2 and 2/3 are different values.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding the same amount to both terms keeps the ratio the same

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I know if 4 : 6 and 10 : 15 are the same ratio?
teach.praise: Divide both terms of each ratio by the same number, and both become 2 : 3. They are equivalent!
teach.nudge: What do you get if you simplify each ratio? What must you do to both terms?

learn.hook: On a map, Delhi to Agra is just 4 cm, but the real road is about 200 km long. Maps work because distances are in proportion!
points: Four numbers are in proportion when a : b = c : d. We write a : b :: c : d.
Cross-multiplication test: a : b :: c : d exactly when a × d = b × c. (Product of extremes = product of means.)
To find a missing term: 3 : 4 :: 12 : x means 3x = 4 × 12 = 48, so x = 16.
Proportion uses multiplication, not addition. Going from 3 to 12 is ×4, so 4 becomes 16 (not 4 + 9 = 13).
A map scale of 1 : 50,000 means 1 cm on the map is 50,000 cm = 500 m on the ground.

example.q: Meena makes 12 laddoos with 2 cups of besan. How much besan does she need for 30 laddoos?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers, cooks, map readers and photo editors all scale things up and down in proportion.

items.text: If a : b :: c : d, then a × d = ___

quiz.q: Are 6, 9, 10, 15 in proportion (6 : 9 :: 10 : 15)?
options: No, because 9 − 6 is not equal to 15 − 10
No, because 10 is not a multiple of 6
Only if they are in rupees
quiz.explain: Product of extremes 6 × 15 = 90 equals product of means 9 × 10 = 90, so they are in proportion. Both ratios equal 2 : 3.
quiz.mistake: Compares differences instead of ratios

quiz.explain: 8 × 7 = 56, so multiply 5 by 7 too: x = 35. Check: 5 × 56 = 280 = 8 × 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds 48 to 5 because 8 + 48 = 56

quiz.q: Meena uses 2 cups of besan for 12 laddoos. How many cups does she need for 30 laddoos?
quiz.explain: 2 : 12 :: x : 30, so 12x = 60 and x = 5 cups.
quiz.mistake: Adds 18 to 2 because 12 + 18 = 30

quiz.q: A map has a scale of 1 : 50,000. Two villages are 6 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they really?
quiz.explain: 6 cm on the map = 6 × 50,000 = 3,00,000 cm. 1 km = 1,00,000 cm, so that is 3 km.
quiz.mistake: Makes a mistake converting cm to km

quiz.q: In a proportion a : b :: c : d, the extremes a and d are 4 and 18, and the mean b is 6. What is the other mean c?
quiz.explain: Product of extremes = product of means: 4 × 18 = 6 × c, so 72 = 6c and c = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which numbers are extremes and which are means

quiz.q: Kabir mixes paint in the ratio 3 parts blue to 2 parts white. He uses 12 litres of blue. How much white does he need?
quiz.explain: Blue went from 3 to 12, that is ×4. So white is 2 × 4 = 8 litres.
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 to 2 because 3 + 9 = 12 (thinks additively)

quiz.q: Which set of numbers is in proportion, taken in the given order?
quiz.mistake: Looks for numbers that increase by the same amount

quiz.q: Aisha's photo is 4 cm wide and 6 cm tall. She enlarges it in proportion so it is 10 cm wide. How tall is it now?
quiz.explain: 4 : 6 :: 10 : h. So 4h = 60 and h = 15 cm. The photo was stretched 2.5 times.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 to both sides (4 + 6 = 10, so 6 + 6 = 12)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How do I check whether 2 : 5 and 6 : 15 are in proportion?
teach.praise: Multiply the outer numbers 2 × 15 and the inner numbers 5 × 6. Both are 30, so yes! Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which numbers should you multiply together? What should be true about the two answers?

topics.title: Unitary method and sharing in a ratio

learn.hook: Is a ₹60 pack of 500 g biscuits a better deal than a ₹84 pack of 750 g? Find the price of the same amount and you will know!
points: Unitary method: first find the value of ONE unit, then multiply for as many units as you need.
5 kg of apples cost ₹600, so 1 kg costs ₹120 and 8 kg cost ₹960.
To compare deals, find the price per gram, per 100 g or per kg. The lower unit price is the better buy.
To divide an amount in the ratio a : b, add the parts (a + b), find one part, then multiply.
₹900 in the ratio 4 : 5: 9 parts, 1 part = ₹100, so the shares are ₹400 and ₹500.

example.q: 3 pens cost ₹45. What do 7 pens cost?

learn.reallife: Comparing prices at a market, splitting a taxi fare, or sharing prize money in a ratio all use the unitary method.

items.q: 4 kg rice cost ₹240. Cost of 1 kg?
A train goes 240 km in 4 hours. km in 1 hour?

games.title: Best buy first
games.prompt: Arrange from cheapest per kg to costliest per kg

quiz.q: 5 kg of apples cost ₹600. What do 8 kg cost?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the total price by 8 without finding the cost of 1 kg

quiz.q: ₹900 is divided between Riya and Arjun in the ratio 4 : 5. How much does Riya get?
quiz.explain: 4 + 5 = 9 parts. 1 part = ₹900 ÷ 9 = ₹100. Riya gets 4 parts = ₹400.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 4 or by 10 instead of by the total number of parts

quiz.q: A 500 g pack of biscuits costs ₹60 and a 750 g pack costs ₹84. Which is the better buy?
options: The 500 g pack, because it costs less money
The 500 g pack, at ₹12 per 100 g
The 750 g pack, at ₹11.20 per 100 g
quiz.explain: 500 g for ₹60 is ₹12 per 100 g. 750 g for ₹84 is ₹84 ÷ 7.5 = ₹11.20 per 100 g. The bigger pack is cheaper per gram.
quiz.mistake: Picks the pack with the lower total price instead of the lower unit price

quiz.q: A train covers 360 km in 6 hours at a steady speed. How far does it go in 4 hours?
quiz.explain: In 1 hour it covers 360 ÷ 6 = 60 km. In 4 hours it covers 4 × 60 = 240 km.
quiz.mistake: Stops at the distance for 1 hour, or divides by 4

quiz.q: Harpreet and Joseph share 42 laddoos in the ratio 3 : 4. How many does Joseph get?
quiz.explain: 3 + 4 = 7 parts. 1 part = 42 ÷ 7 = 6 laddoos. Joseph gets 4 × 6 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Gives Harpreet's share (18) instead of Joseph's

quiz.q: 12 notebooks cost ₹540. What does one notebook cost?
quiz.explain: One notebook costs ₹540 ÷ 12 = ₹45.
quiz.mistake: Makes a division slip, for example 540 ÷ 10

quiz.q: A recipe needs 250 g of sugar for 4 people. How much sugar is needed for 10 people?
quiz.explain: For 1 person: 250 ÷ 4 = 62.5 g. For 10 people: 10 × 62.5 = 625 g.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 250 by 10 without first finding the amount for 1 person

quiz.q: ₹1200 is divided among three friends in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the largest share?
quiz.explain: 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 parts. 1 part = ₹1200 ÷ 6 = ₹200. The largest share is 3 parts = ₹600.
quiz.mistake: Divides equally by 3 friends (₹400 each)

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 4 samosas cost ₹60. How do I find what 7 samosas cost?
teach.praise: First one samosa: ₹60 ÷ 4 = ₹15. Then 7 × ₹15 = ₹105. The unitary method is yummy!
teach.nudge: What should you find first, before working out 7 samosas?

learn.hook: A Diwali sale banner says '25% OFF'. That is just a fraction wearing a disguise: 25/100, which is one quarter off!
points: Per cent means 'per hundred'. 35% = 35/100 = 0.35.
To change a fraction to a percentage, multiply by 100: 3/4 = 3/4 × 100% = 75%, and 1/8 = 12.5%.
x% of a quantity = quantity × x/100. So 20% of ₹450 = ₹450 × 20/100 = ₹90.
What percentage is a of b? Work out a/b × 100. Getting 18 out of 24 is 18/24 × 100 = 75%.
Finding the whole: if 30% of a number is 45, the number is 45 × 100/30 = 150.

example.q: Kabir scored 42 out of 60 in a quiz. What percentage did he score?

learn.reallife: Marks in exams, battery levels on a phone, the chance of rain and interest in a bank are all shown as percentages.

quiz.q: What is 35% as a fraction in simplest form?
quiz.explain: 35% = 35/100. Divide top and bottom by 5 to get 7/20.
quiz.mistake: Simplifies wrongly or forgets that per cent means out of 100

quiz.q: Riya scored 42 out of 60 in a test. What percentage did she score?
quiz.mistake: Writes the marks scored as the percentage without dividing by the total

quiz.q: What is 20% of ₹450?
quiz.mistake: Finds 10% instead of 20%, or subtracts 20 from 450

quiz.q: Write 3/8 as a percentage.
quiz.mistake: Writes the decimal 0.375 with a % sign without multiplying by 100

quiz.q: In a school, 30% of the students come by bus. If 45 students come by bus, how many students are there in the school?
quiz.explain: 30% of the total is 45, so 1% is 45 ÷ 30 = 1.5 and 100% is 150.
quiz.mistake: Finds 30% of 45 (13.5) instead of the whole

quiz.q: Which of these has the largest value: 5/8, 0.6, 61%, 0.59?
quiz.explain: Turn all into decimals: 5/8 = 0.625, 0.6, 61% = 0.61, 0.59. So 5/8 is the largest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 61% is largest because 61 is a big number

quiz.q: A cricket team won 18 out of 24 matches and lost the rest. What percentage of matches did it lose?
quiz.mistake: Gives the winning percentage (75%) instead of the losing percentage

quiz.q: Meena spends 40% of her ₹500 pocket money on books. How much money is left?
quiz.explain: She spends 40% and keeps 60%. 60% of ₹500 = ₹300.
quiz.mistake: Gives the amount spent instead of the amount left

teach.ask: Gappu asks: What does 25% really mean? Is it 25 rupees?
teach.praise: 25% means 25 out of every 100, which is the fraction 25/100 = 1/4. Not always 25 rupees! Thanks!
teach.nudge: What does 'per cent' mean? Can you write 25% as a fraction?

learn.hook: Your height grew from 140 cm to 147 cm and your little cousin's from 70 cm to 77 cm. Both grew 7 cm, but who grew more in percentage?
points: Percentage change = (change ÷ original value) × 100.
Always divide by the ORIGINAL (starting) value, not the new value.
Increase by r%: new value = original × (100 + r)/100. So ₹200 up by 10% = ₹200 × 1.1 = ₹220.
Decrease by r%: new value = original × (100 − r)/100. So ₹500 down by 20% = ₹500 × 0.8 = ₹400.
Up 10% then down 10% does NOT bring you back: 100 → 110 → 99.

example.q: A cricket bat's price rose from ₹800 to ₹1000. Find the percentage increase.

learn.reallife: News reports say things like 'petrol price up 5%' or 'school enrolment up 12%'. Percent change lets us compare fairly.

items.text: ₹200 increased by 10% = ₹___
₹500 decreased by 20% = ₹___
Going from 40 to 50 is a ___ increase
Going from 50 to 40 is a ___ decrease

games.title: Percent puzzles
items: Going from 40 to 50 and going from 50 to 40 are the same percentage change.
Increasing by 10% and then decreasing by 10% brings you back to the start.
A 100% increase means the amount doubles.
Adding 100% of the amount adds the whole amount again.
To increase a number by 25%, you can multiply it by 1.25.
Percentage change is found by dividing the change by the new value.
We always divide by the original value.

quiz.q: The price of a cricket bat rose from ₹800 to ₹1000. What is the percentage increase?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new price (200/1000 = 20%)

quiz.q: A village has 5000 people. The population grows by 8%. What is the new population?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 instead of 8%

quiz.q: A school bag costs ₹1200. Its price is reduced by 15%. What is the new price?
quiz.mistake: Gives only the reduction (₹180) or adds it

quiz.q: Aisha's marks went down from 60 to 45. What is the percentage decrease?
quiz.explain: Decrease = 15. Divide by the original 60: 15/60 = 1/4 = 25%.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new value 45 (gets 33 1/3%)

quiz.q: Start with 100. Increase it by 10%, then decrease the result by 10%. What is the final number?
quiz.explain: 100 + 10% = 110. Then 10% of 110 is 11, and 110 − 11 = 99. The second 10% is of a bigger number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two 10% changes cancel out

quiz.q: A train ticket costs ₹400 after a 25% increase. What was the original price?
quiz.explain: New price = 125% of original. So original = 400 × 100/125 = ₹320. Check: 25% of 320 = 80, and 320 + 80 = 400.
quiz.mistake: Takes 25% off ₹400 (gets ₹300), but the 25% was of the original price

quiz.q: A shop sold 250 boxes of diyas last Diwali and 400 boxes this Diwali. What is the percentage increase?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the new value 400 (37.5%) or gives the increase itself

quiz.q: To decrease a price by 30%, you can multiply it by which number?
quiz.explain: After a 30% decrease, 70% of the price is left. 70% = 0.7.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 0.3, which gives the decrease instead of the new price

teach.ask: Gappu asks: Something went from 40 to 50. How do I find the percentage increase?
teach.praise: The change is 10, divide by the original 40, and multiply by 100: 25%. Perfect!
teach.nudge: First find how much it changed. Then which number do you divide by: 40 or 50?

learn.hook: A shopkeeper marks a kurta at ₹800, gives a 20% discount, and still makes a profit. How? It cost him only ₹500!
points: Cost price (CP) is what the seller paid. Selling price (SP) is what the buyer pays.
If SP > CP there is a profit: Profit = SP − CP. If CP > SP there is a loss: Loss = CP − SP.
Profit % and loss % are always worked out on the cost price: Profit % = Profit/CP × 100.
Marked price (MP) is the price on the tag. Discount = MP − SP, and discount % is worked out on the marked price.
After a discount of r%, SP = MP × (100 − r)/100.

learn.hook: More than 2500 years ago, the Indian mathematician Baudhayana wrote down a rule for building fire altars that we still use to find distances today!
points: A right triangle has one angle of 90°. The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse, and it is the longest side.
The Baudhayana–Pythagoras theorem: if the legs are a and b and the hypotenuse is c, then a² + b² = c².
In Baudhayana's words (roughly): the diagonal of a rectangle makes a square as big as the squares on its length and breadth put together.
To find the hypotenuse: c = √(a² + b²). To find a leg: a = √(c² − b²).
Converse: if the sides of a triangle satisfy a² + b² = c², then the angle opposite c is a right angle.

example.q: A 13 m ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 5 m from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
steps: The ladder is the hypotenuse: c = 13
One leg is 5, let the height be h

learn.reallife: Firefighters placing ladders, TV makers measuring screen size along the diagonal, and pilots finding straight-line distances all use this theorem.

quiz.explain: The ladder is the hypotenuse. Height² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the height is 12 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the squares instead of subtracting, or forgets the square root

quiz.mistake: Thinks the side drawn at the bottom (base) is always the longest

quiz.q: Riya walks 9 m east and then 12 m north. How far is she from her starting point in a straight line?
quiz.explain: East and north make a right angle. Distance² = 9² + 12² = 81 + 144 = 225, so the distance is 15 m.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two distances walked (21 m)

quiz.q: A TV screen is 80 cm wide and 60 cm tall. How long is its diagonal?
quiz.explain: Diagonal² = 80² + 60² = 6400 + 3600 = 10,000, so the diagonal is 100 cm.
quiz.mistake: Adds the width and height instead of using squares

quiz.q: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of 25 cm and one leg of 24 cm. How long is the other leg?
quiz.explain: Other leg² = 25² − 24² = 625 − 576 = 49, so it is 7 cm.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the sides (25 − 24 = 1) instead of their squares

quiz.q: The squares on the two legs of a right triangle have areas 36 cm² and 64 cm². What is the area of the square on the hypotenuse?
quiz.explain: The theorem says the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the legs: 36 + 64 = 100 cm².
quiz.mistake: Gives the side length (10) instead of the area, or subtracts

quiz.q: In triangle PQR, ∠Q = 90°. Which equation is correct?
quiz.explain: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle at Q, so it is PR. Then PR² = PQ² + QR².
quiz.mistake: Does not find the side opposite the right angle first

teach.ask: Gappu asks: A right triangle has legs 3 and 4. How do I find the long side?
teach.praise: Square the legs: 9 and 16. Add: 25. Square root: 5! Baudhayana would be proud!
teach.nudge: What do you do to 3 and 4 first? And after adding, how do you get back to a length?

learn.hook: 3, 4, 5 is a magic trio: 9 + 16 = 25. Are there more such trios? Infinitely many!
points: A Pythagorean triple is three whole numbers a, b, c with a² + b² = c². The smallest is (3, 4, 5).
Multiply a triple by any whole number to get another: (6, 8, 10), (9, 12, 15), (30, 40, 50).
Some triples are not multiples of smaller ones: (5, 12, 13), (8, 15, 17), (7, 24, 25), (20, 21, 29).
A recipe: for any whole number m > 1, the numbers 2m, m² − 1 and m² + 1 form a triple. For m = 4: 8, 15, 17.
To test a triple, square the two smaller numbers, add them, and compare with the square of the largest.

example.q: Is (20, 21, 29) a Pythagorean triple?

learn.reallife: Carpenters and tile layers use triples like 6-8-10 to check that corners are truly square.

quiz.q: Which of these is a Pythagorean triple?
quiz.mistake: Picks numbers that just look close together

quiz.q: Complete the Pythagorean triple (9, 40, __).
quiz.mistake: Adds 9 and 40 instead of their squares

quiz.q: Using 2m, m² − 1 and m² + 1 with m = 7, what is the largest number of the triple?
quiz.mistake: Uses m² (49) without adding 1

quiz.q: (3, 4, 5) is a triple. Which of these is also a triple made by multiplying it?
quiz.explain: (15, 20, 25) = 5 × (3, 4, 5). Multiplying every number by the same amount keeps a² + b² = c².
quiz.mistake: Adds the same number to each, or multiplies only some of the numbers

quiz.q: A right triangle has legs 10 cm and 24 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
quiz.mistake: Uses the triple (5, 12, 13) but forgets to double 13

quiz.q: Harpreet's triangle has sides 7 cm, 24 cm and 25 cm. Is it a right triangle?
options: Yes, because 25 is the longest side
quiz.explain: 49 + 576 = 625 = 25². By the converse of the theorem, the triangle has a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Adds the sides instead of their squares

quiz.q: In the Pythagorean triple (20, 21, x), what is x?
